q_45090.question_text: The winner of the 2026 Air Guitar World Championships will be from where?
q_45090.reasoning:
(a) **Time left until resolution:**
The competition final is August 28-29, 2026. Today is August 5, 2026. Resolution will occur in approximately 23-24 days.

(b) **Most likely outcome and why:**

The field for the 2026 Air Guitar World Championships final consists of national champions from 12 countries/regions:
- Europe: The Netherlands, France, Germany, Belgium, UK, Finland (6 competitors)
- North America: USA, Canada (2 competitors)
- Asia: Japan, Taiwan (2 competitors)
- South America: Brazil (1 competitor)

**Historical base rate:** Looking at the resolution example, the 2025 winner was from Finland (Europe). The Air Guitar World Championships have been held in Oulu, Finland since 1996, meaning 30 years of history. Europe has hosted this event continuously, and there is likely a strong base rate of European winners, particularly Finnish winners given home advantage.

**Current advantage factors:**
- Home advantage: Finland has the reigning champion (Aapo "The Angus" Rautio) and is hosting. Home advantage in performance competitions is typically significant.
- European representation: 6 of 12 finalists are European (50% of the field), making Europe the largest represented continent.
- Historical precedent: The 2025 winner was European (Finnish specifically).

**Considerations against other options:**
- North America (USA, Canada): 2 of 12 finalists (17%)
- Asia (Japan, Taiwan): 2 of 12 finalists (17%)
- "Somewhere else" (Brazil): 1 of 12 finalists (8%)

Europe has both the largest representation (50%) and historical precedent of winning at this venue. The reigning champion being Finnish and the event being in Finland provides additional home-field advantage.

(c) **Key uncertainties:**

The main uncertainty is performance outcome - this is a subjective artistic competition where an outsider could theoretically win if they deliver an exceptionally compelling performance. However, the structural advantages (home field, largest contingent, historical precedent) point strongly toward Europe.

**Probability assessment:**

Given:
- Europe represents 50% of the finalist pool (6 of 12)
- Home advantage for Finland specifically (reigning champion, hosting)
- Historical base rate showing European (particularly Finnish) dominance
- The subjective nature of the competition means outsiders could win, but the odds favor the largest/home contingent

Europe is heavily favored. A reasonable distribution:
- **Europe: 70%** (home advantage, largest contingent, historical precedent)
- **North America: 15%** (2 competitors, 17% of field)
- **Asia: 12%** (2 competitors, 17% of field)
- **Somewhere else: 3%** (Brazil, 1 competitor, 8% of field)

This allocates roughly proportional to representation with adjustment for home advantage and historical pattern.

Option probabilities:
Europe: 70%
North America: 15%
Asia: 12%
Somewhere else: 3%
q_45090.research_text: The 2026 Air Guitar World Championships will take place in Oulu, Finland, from August 26–29, 2026, as part of the Delta Life grand finale within Oulu's year as the European Capital of Culture [airguitarworldchampionships.com](https://airguitarworldchampionships.com/en/home/), [oulunjuhlaviikot.fi](https://www.oulunjuhlaviikot.fi/en/main-event/air-guitar-world-championships/). The reigning world champion, Aapo "The Angus" Rautio from Finland, will be challenged by national champions from 11 countries: The Netherlands, USA, Canada, France, Germany, Belgium, UK, Japan, Taiwan, Brazil, and Finland [airguitarworldchampionships.com](https://airguitarworldchampionships.com/en/national-championships-published/). The competition will include a two-day final on August 28 and 29, 2026, held at the Delta Stage in Pokkinen park, Oulu, with free entry and a live stream available [airguitarworldchampionships.com](https://airguitarworldchampionships.com/en/program/world-final/), [oulunjuhlaviikot.fi](https://www.oulunjuhlaviikot.fi/en/main-event/air-guitar-world-championships/). The winner will receive a unique "Flying Finn" guitar [airguitarworldchampionships.com](https://airguitarworldchampionships.com/en/program/world-final/).
